tweets: SWC-105 notes this bug is sometimes caused by unintentionally exposing initialization functions.
Due to missing or insufficient access controls, malicious parties can withdraw some or all Ether from the contract account.
By wrongly naming a function intended to be a constructor, the constructor code ends up in the runtime byte code.
The exposed code can be called by anyone to re-initialize the contract, potentially allowing withdrawal of Ether.
Reviewers should check if only the constructor executes during deployment and no other init logic remains public.
